topic.name: The Sum of the First N Terms of a Geometric Series

question.text: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the first term is $42$ and the common ratio is $-\dfrac{1}{5}?$
question.explanation:
The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

\[ S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r}. \]

In this case, $a_1= 42$ and $r = -\dfrac{1}{5}.$ Therefore, we have:

\begin{align} S_N &= \dfrac{42\left[1-\left(-\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^N\right]}{1-\left(-\dfrac{1}{5}\right)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{42\left[1-\left(-\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^N\right]}{\dfrac{6}{5}} \\[5pt] &= 35\left[1-\left(-\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^N\right] \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Formula for the Sum of a Geometric Series Given the First Term and Common Ratio

question.text: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $2+18+162+\cdots?$
question.explanation:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

\begin{align} r &= \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{18}{2}\\[5pt] &= 9 \end{align}

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

\[ S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r}. \]

In this case $a_1=2$ and $r=9.$ Substituting these values into the formula for $S_N$ gives the following:

\begin{align} S_N &=\dfrac{a_1(1-r^N)}{1-r} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2\left(1-9^N\right)}{1-9} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2\left(1-9^N\right)}{(-8)} \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{1}{4}\left(1-9^N\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{4}\left(9^N-1\right) \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Formula for the Sum of a Geometric Series Given the First Few Terms

question.text: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $4$th term is $192$ and the common ratio is $4?$
question.explanation:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine $a_1\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} a_n &= a_1r^{n-1} \\[3pt] 192 &= a_1\cdot 4^{\left(4-1\right)} \\[3pt] 192 &= 64 a_1 \\[3pt] a_1 &= 3 \end{align}

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

\[ S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r} . \]

In this case, $a_1=3$ and $r=4.$ Substituting our values into the formula for $S_N$ gives:

\begin{align} S_N &= \dfrac{3(1-4^N)}{1-4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{(-3)}(1-4^N) \\[5pt] &= -(1-4^N) \\[5pt] &= 4^N-1 \end{align}
